[Executive Jet Management](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airlines/EJM)
 (EJM, [Cincinnati Lunken](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airports/4382)
) retired the sole Phenom 300 from its Part 135-certified fleet in December 2024, ch-aviation research reveals.

N577JM (msn 50500301) was last active under Executive Jet Management's 'EJM' code on December 3, completing a test flight around [Dallas Love Field](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airports/4427)
, following a flight from [San Francisco](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airports/5078)
. The 9.6-year-old aircraft, operated by the company since May 2024, is currently not listed as Part 135-certified.

With the retirement of the Phenom 300, Executive Jet Management continues to operate other [Embraer Executive Jets](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airlines/EEJ)
, including a [Praetor 600](https://www.ch-aviation.com/aircraft-data/ET6)
, two [Legacy 600](https://www.ch-aviation.com/aircraft-variants/LEGA600)
s, and a [Legacy 650](https://www.ch-aviation.com/aircraft-variants/LEGA650)
, alongside 160 other jets manufactured by [Bombardier Business Aircraft](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airlines/BOJ)
, [Dassault Aviation](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airlines/DAZ)
, [Gulfstream Aerospace](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airlines/GUL)
, and [Textron Aviation](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airlines/TXT)
.

The company is a subsidiary of [NetJets Aviation](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airlines/EJA)
, which operates 117 Phenom 300 and Phenom 300E aircraft under the Part 135 certificate of its United States division, as well as 28 additional aircraft of the same variants with its Portuguese unit, [NetJets Transportes Aéreos](https://www.ch-aviation.com/airlines/NJE)
.
